title: Weight Loss Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Weight Loss Calculator: Daily calories and a realistic timeline to reach your goal weight. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and…
content:
The [Weight Loss Calculator](/weight-loss-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Daily calories and a realistic timeline to reach your goal weight. Enter your sex, age, height, current weight, goal weight, activity level and planned loss per week and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Work out how many calories to eat each day to reach a goal weight, and how long it should take. The calculator finds your maintenance calories from the Mifflin-St Jeor equation (basal metabolic rate times your activity level), then subtracts a daily deficit based on your planned loss — one kilogram of body fat stores about 7,700 kcal, so losing 0.5 kg a week needs a 550 kcal daily deficit. This is an estimate for healthy adults, not medical advice: it does not suit children, pregnancy, eating disorders or anyone with a medical condition, and a daily target under 1,200 kcal (women) or 1,500 kcal (men) should only be planned with a professional.

## How to use the Weight Loss Calculator

Start by choosing your sex from the list, then entering your age, entering your height (cm), entering your current weight (kg), entering your goal weight (kg), choosing your activity level from the list and finally choosing your planned loss per week from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter your sex, age, height and current weight.
2. Enter your goal weight and your activity level.
3. Choose how fast to lose — 0.5 kg a week is the usual steady rate.
4. Read your target daily calories and the estimated weeks to your goal.

## Formula

BMR (Mifflin-St Jeor): men 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age + 5; women the same with −161. Maintenance = BMR × activity factor. Daily deficit = weekly loss × 7,700 ÷ 7. Target = maintenance − deficit. Weeks = (current − goal) ÷ weekly loss.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Weight Loss Calculator](/weight-loss-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A 30-year-old man, 180 cm, 90 kg, moderately active, aiming for 80 kg at 0.5 kg a week: basal metabolic rate is 1,880 kcal, maintenance is 2,914 kcal a day, the target is 2,364 kcal a day (a 550 kcal deficit), and the goal takes about 20 weeks. Try the same figures in the [Weight Loss Calculator](/weight-loss-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Sex: Male, Age: 30, Height: 180 cm, Current weight: 90 kg, Goal weight: 80 kg, Activity level: Moderate (3–5 days/week), Planned loss per week: 0.5 kg/week (steady)), the [Weight Loss Calculator](/weight-loss-calculator) returns Maintenance calories: 2,914 kcal/day, Target daily calories: 2,364 kcal/day, Daily calorie deficit: 550 kcal/day, Weight to lose: 10 kg, Estimated time to goal: 20 weeks, Safety check: Within the usual safe range. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Why 0.5 kg a week is the usual advice

Losing 0.5 kg a week needs a 550 kcal daily deficit, which most people can manage by eating a little less and moving a little more. Faster loss needs a bigger deficit, which is harder to sustain and more likely to cost muscle as well as fat. Weight loss also slows over time: as you get lighter your maintenance calories fall, so the same daily intake produces a smaller deficit. Expect plateaus, and re-check your target every few kilograms.

## What the estimate cannot see

The Mifflin-St Jeor equation is the most accurate general formula, but it still misses by 10% or more for very muscular or very unfit people, because it estimates from weight and height rather than body composition. Water, glycogen and food in the gut can swing the scale by a kilogram day to day — weigh yourself at the same time of day, several times a week, and trust the trend over two or three weeks, not any single reading.

## When to get professional help

See a doctor or registered dietitian before starting if you have diabetes, heart disease, thyroid problems, a history of eating disorders, are pregnant, or if the calculator puts your target under 1,200 kcal (women) or 1,500 kcal (men). Rapid weight loss, dizziness or constant fatigue are signs to stop and get advice.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Weigh yourself at the same time of day and watch the two-week trend, not daily swings.
- Keep protein up while you lose weight — it protects muscle and keeps you full.
- If progress stalls for three weeks, re-check your target: your maintenance has fallen as you got lighter.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many calories should I eat to lose weight?

Maintenance calories minus a deficit. For 0.5 kg a week, subtract about 550 kcal a day from maintenance. This calculator works out both numbers from your age, sex, height, weight and activity. Try it with your own numbers in the [Weight Loss Calculator](/weight-loss-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How fast can I safely lose weight?

Most guidance says 0.5–1 kg a week. Faster than that is harder to sustain and more likely to lose muscle as well as fat — and very low-calorie plans should only be done with professional supervision. Try it with your own numbers in the [Weight Loss Calculator](/weight-loss-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why has my weight loss stopped?

Usually because maintenance calories fall as you get lighter, so the original deficit shrinks. Re-run the calculator at your new weight, and check that portions and activity have not drifted. Try it with your own numbers in the [Weight Loss Calculator](/weight-loss-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Weight Loss Calculator use?

BMR (Mifflin-St Jeor): men 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age + 5; women the same with −161. Maintenance = BMR × activity factor. Daily deficit = weekly loss × 7,700 ÷ 7. Target = maintenance − deficit. Weeks = (current − goal) ÷ weekly loss.
